notes:
Minnesota's recurring entity-level charge is the minimum fee of M.S. 290.0922: an annual tax imposed on every partnership-taxed filer (a default multi-member LLC included) in addition to any income tax, owed to the Department of Revenue with the partnership return. It is in under this namespace's substance test on the New York precedent: keyed to the entity's Minnesota presence, paid by the entity, recurring - the state calling it a fee does not make it the annual report's filing fee, which in Minnesota is the Secretary of State's free annual renewal.
basis is composite, the enum value this record added: the fee scales with the sum of Minnesota property, payrolls, and sales or receipts - neither net worth nor revenue alone. The schedule is stepped, with a published $0 bottom tier below the first threshold, so minimumAnnualUsd is 0 in the Texas/Ohio sense of a real zero. The dollar amounts quoted are statutory-year-2019 figures that the commissioner indexes annually; the current-year brackets are larger and are published on the Department's minimum fee page, which this session could not read (below).
A partnership deriving over 80 percent of its income from farming is exempt. firstYearExemption is false: the tax is imposed for each taxable year with no first-year carve-out.
collectedWithAnnualReport is false. Root states.json carries annual_report_fee 0 - the Secretary of State's annual renewal is free for a domestic LLC in good standing - and the minimum fee is a different payment to a different agency.
A single-member LLC disregarded for federal tax purposes is outside 290.0922(b)'s partnership-return filers; its owner reports the income directly. The record describes the default multi-member case, the same posture the other records take.
stateIncomeTax: members owe Minnesota income tax on pass-through income at graduated rates topping at 9.85 percent (M.S. 290.06, subd. 2c), and 289A.08, subd. 7a gives a partnership-taxed LLC a pass-through entity tax election.
This is a statute-only record by necessity, the Ohio shape: every deep path on www.revenue.state.mn.us - the minimum fee instructions, income tax rates, the PTE tax page, even the home page - answers a scripted client with a Radware Bot Manager captcha via validate.perfdrive.com, a 200 that is not the page, measured on the VPN-down route on 2026-08-07. The Revisor of Statutes carries every value the schema needs.
needsReview: Two loose ends, neither a value in doubt. (1) The current-year indexed minimum fee brackets and thresholds are not recorded: the statute fixes only the statutory-year-2019 amounts and the commissioner's adjusted figures live on www.revenue.state.mn.us, which serves a Radware captcha to every scripted request on this route; a browser session could read the minimum fee page against a snapshot, or a VPN-up session should re-probe the host. The $0 bottom tier and the record's other values do not depend on the indexed figures. (2) The www.revenue.state.mn.us wall was measured on the VPN-down route only; whether the up route clears it is unmeasured.
